messages:
Laura: Quick sync — we need to settle on the controlplane pairing protocol for Private deployments. The current plan uses a one-time pairing token + ephemeral TLS cert exchange. Questions about retries and idempotency came up.
Aj: Are we still leaning on short-lived tokens (60s) that are redeemed once and bound to a CP instance? Concern: NAT retries and duplicate redemption if client resends during network flaps.
Mike: I worry about lost acks. If client retries, the token might have been consumed and the second attempt should be safe to treat as success, not fail. We need idempotent semantics.
Olivia: Proposal: token redeem -> server returns pairing-id + cert chain + stable instance-id. Client stores pairing-id and retries can pass pairing-id to confirm prior success. If pairing-id exists, server returns 200 with same cert metadata.
Sam: That sounds fine, but what about replay attacks? pairing-id must be unguessable and tied to the original token and source IP/nonce.
Laura: Agreed. Add a short binding: pairing-id = HMAC(token || client-nonce || cp-instance-id) with server-side TTL. Also store client nonce to prevent simple replay.
Aj: TTL tradeoff: long TTL = easier retries but longer window if leaked. Short TTL + retry window might be better. Suggest default 5m pairing window, token validity 60s for initial redeem.
Mike: We should document exact state machine. Rough sketch:

```
client -> controlplane: POST /pairings {token, client_nonce}
server: mark token redeemed if valid, create pairing-id, return pairing-id, certs
client on retry -> POST /pairings/verify {pairing-id}
server: if pairing-id valid -> return same certs (idempotent)
```

Olivia: Also need a safe path if server completed provisioning but cert issuance is async. Client might time out but pairing succeeded. So verify endpoint must be cheap and eventually consistent.
Sam: What about NAT / port translations that change client IP? Binding to IP will break some clients. Maybe bind to client nonce + token only, but rate-limit reuse.
Laura: Good point — don't tie to IP, tie to client_nonce and token and maybe TLS public key fingerprint.
Aj: Retry semantics: client should do exponential backoff and include a Retry-ID header (UUID) on all attempts. Server can dedupe by token + Retry-ID.
Mike: We should support idempotent retry window of ~2m for dedupe by Retry-ID, and a longer pairing lookup by pairing-id for late-checks (5m). These values are configurable per customer.
Olivia: Operationally, we need metrics: pairing_attempts, pairing_success, pairing_retries_deduped, pairing_time_ms, pairing_async_completions. Also alert when failure rate > 1% for 10m.
Laura: Security: rotate the signing key every week? That's high churn. Maybe weekly for short-lived certs is ok if we automate rollover and keep previous key for verifying within 1h grace.
Sam: KMS-backed keys + automated rolling is required for Private deployments. Document GracePeriod = 1h.
Aj: Fallback behavior: if pairing fails repeatedly, client should fallback to regional relay with reduced capability. Make this explicit in SDKs.
Mike: SDK contract:
- expose pairing() with callbacks for success/fail/verify
- auto-retry with jitter
- expose pairing_id and certs to host app
- expose fallback_to_relay boolean

Olivia: We also need an operator command to forcibly revoke pairing-ids for a tenant (support rotation or incident response). API: DELETE /pairings/{pairing-id}?force=true
Laura: For compatibility, older controlplanes may not support verify endpoint. Server should respond 404 -> client then falls back to token-based probing and logs a telemetry event.
Sam: Edge case: partial provisioning where instance recorded pairing but failed to apply cert. Add a pending state and reconciliation job that retries cert application and marks pairing completed once cert observed.
Aj: Can we reuse existing rollout work for canary pairing? e.g., gradually enable strict binding for a subset of customers. Tagging in the CP config: pairing_mode = strict|lenient.
Mike: Implementation notes:
- store redeemed tokens in Dynamo-like store with TTL index
- pairing-ids in a separate table keyed by pairing-id with token reference + state
- fast lookup by token for dedupe
- metrics emitted via statsd

Laura: Ops checklist before rollout:
- run spike with lenient mode for 48h
- collect pairing_retries_deduped rate
- enable strict mode behind feature flag per region
- verify KMS rotation automation

Olivia: Any objections to these defaults? (60s token, 2m dedupe window, 5m pairing lookup, 1h key grace)
Aj: 👍 on defaults, but make everything configurable per-tenant.
Mike: Add note: documented backup path for customers behind very flaky networks: allow longer pairing lookup (up to 24h) with explicit opt-in.
Laura: Thanks. I'll draft a short follow-up RFC with the state machine and example SDK snippets. Will include sample logs and error codes (409 for redeemed, 404 verify not-supported, 410 for expired).
infra-bot: Deploy preview for /pairings endpoint available at: https://staging-api.internal/pairings (expires in 2h)
Sam: I'll spin up a test harness to simulate retries and NAT changes. Ping me if you need test tokens. :rocket:
Laura: Great — target RFC by EOD tomorrow.
